# CreatePlane <img class="product" src="media/b3d-20x14.png" alt="Blitz3D" title="Blitz3D" width="20" height="14">

<div align="center">

[Command Index](Command-Index) · [Blitz3D](Blitz3D) · [Meshes](Blitz3D-Meshes)

</div>


```blitzbasic
CreatePlane:Int32 segments:Int32=1, parent:Int32=0
```

| Parameter | Mode | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `segments` | In | Int32 | `1` | How many pieces the plane is divided into per side, 1 or more. 0 or less counts as 1. Defaults to 1. |
| `parent` | In | Int32 | `0` | Entity the plane follows, or 0 for none. Defaults to 0. |

**Returns:** The handle of the new plane.

## Description

Creates a flat, endless ground at height 0 that faces up. It is handy for outdoor scenes where the player should never see an edge. The plane is one-sided, so it is not seen from below. More `segments` split it into smaller squares, which gives lights and fog more vertices to work with and hides problems some graphics cards have with big flat triangles.

## Differences

* The original allows 1 to 16 segments, and larger values can crash it or stop it with an error. Here there is no upper limit, but every segment more makes each frame a little slower, as the visible part of the plane is built again for every frame.
* Collisions and picks see the plane as one square 20000 units wide, so they miss it further out than that. Drawing is not limited: the part of the plane that a camera sees is made again for every frame.

## Examples

```blitzbasic
Graphics3D 320, 240, 0, 2
SetBuffer BackBuffer()
camera = CreateCamera()
PositionEntity camera, 0, 2, -6
RotateEntity camera, 12, 0, 0
CameraClsColor camera, 150, 190, 230
light = CreateLight()
RotateEntity light, 50, 30, 0
ground = CreatePlane()
EntityColor ground, 70, 140, 70
box = CreateCube()
PositionEntity box, 0, 1, 2
RenderWorld
Flip
WaitKey
```
